extracted.intended_audience: researchers invited to peer review manuscripts for PLOS Pathogens
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for scientists performing peer review for PLOS Pathogens, covering whether to accept invitations, how to assess manuscripts against publication criteria, how to write reviews, and editorial handling of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting reviewer invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept an invitation only if you have the knowledge, time and objectivity necessary to provide an unbiased assessment of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use links in the invitation email or Editorial Manager to accept/decline. If you accept, you also give permission to publish your review under a Creative Commons Attribution CC BY license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Pathogens practices single-anonymized peer review by default (you will know the authors' names; your name will not be shared).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your review will appear in the editorial decision letter and can be read by the authors and other reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: You can choose to sign your name to your review when you submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you sign, authors and other reviewers will see your name; if authors publish their peer review history, your name will accompany your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may accompany manuscripts transferred to other PLOS journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to have your review considered by editors at another PLOS journal; you may be asked to re-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published peer review history
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors choose to publish peer review history, the editorial decision letter and your review may appear alongside the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your name will not appear unless you chose to sign the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interest is anything that interferes with or could be perceived as potentially interfering with a thorough and objective assessment of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common examples: recent/current collaboration with authors; direct competition or history of scientific conflict; opportunity to profit financially. Do not accept the assignment if you have a competing interest or cannot be objective. If unsure, contact the journal office. If asked to review despite a competing interest, declare it when you submit your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crediting collaborators who helped the review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you had help completing the review you must share your collaborator’s name with the journal when you submit the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the collaborator's name in the 'Confidential comments to the Editor' field or email the journal. Do not include the collaborator's name in the text of the review itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of manuscripts and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscripts and correspondence confidential and do not share information about submissions with anyone else unless previously agreed with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not make use of any material or take advantage of information gained through the peer review process. See the PLOS Confidentiality Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing a manuscript previously reviewed elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: If you reviewed the article at another journal, consider the manuscript as a new submission unless instructed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind it may have been revised; PLOS Pathogens’ criteria for publication may differ. When submitting your review, tell the editor if you reviewed a previous version at another journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to complete review
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to complete your review within 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time, email the journal as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving reviewer credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Review activity can be recorded and credited via ORCID and Publons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link your PLOS reviewer account to ORCID or Publons and set up syncing to post review activity to your ORCID profile. This confirms you completed a review but does not publish the content of your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct and scientific validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be ethically conducted and scientifically valid to be eligible for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to ethics/validity, manuscripts must also meet the journal's specific publication criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing originality, consider whether the claims are novel and which published articles might weaken the originality claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance to researchers in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be of high importance to researchers in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the significance of the main claims for the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance and broad interest to pathogen research community
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should have high importance and broad interest to the community studying pathogens and pathogen–host interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the likely interest across the community, not only to narrow specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should use rigorous methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate study design, controls, statistical analysis, and whether methods are appropriate and robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial evidence for conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be substantial evidence supporting the manuscript's conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the data and analyses fully support the claims and what additional evidence, if any, is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify main claims and significance in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should state the main claims of the paper and how significant they are for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an expert opinion on the validity and quality of the manuscript and explicit feedback to help authors improve the paper to meet journal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess novelty explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims are novel and identify published work that weakens originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are not novel, cite specific published articles that undermine originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize with previous literature and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if the claims are properly placed in the context of previous literature and whether the authors treated the literature fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out omissions or misrepresentations of prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether data and analyses support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess if the data and analyses fully support the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not, specify what other evidence is required and whether additional experiments/analyses would improve the paper and how difficult they would be to perform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend additional work when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether additional work would improve the paper and estimate how much better the paper would be and the difficulty of that work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether revisions are necessary and whether they are feasible within a reasonable timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend publishing detailed protocols/algorithms as supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS encourages authors to publish detailed protocols and algorithms as supporting information online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If particular methods warrant such treatment, suggest this. If a protocol is provided (e.g., RCT), check for deviations and ask authors to explain them adequately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original data deposition and accession numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Original data should be deposited in appropriate repositories and accession/version numbers provided for genes, proteins, mutants, diseases, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that deposition has occurred and that accession numbers are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to relevant reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies should conform to relevant guidelines such as CONSORT, MIAME, QUORUM, STROBE, and the Fort Lauderdale agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess conformity and request adherence or explanation for deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological detail sufficient for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Details of the methodology should be sufficient to allow the experiments to be reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request additional methodological detail where necessary and note any irreproducible elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any software created by the authors should be freely available where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether software is available and usable; request access or clarification if not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript organization and clarity for non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should be well organized and written clearly enough to be accessible to non-specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If clarity is insufficient, recommend language editing or suggest the authors seek a professional science writer and notify the journal office if you think this is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and explanation of standardized nomenclature and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper should use standardized scientific nomenclature and abbreviations, or explain them at first usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out non-standard terms and request explanations or standardization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag experiments using select agents or toxins
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the manuscript describes experiments using a select agent or toxin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the journal's list of select agents and ensure appropriate oversight and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag NIH-defined Dual Use concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if, in your opinion, the manuscript contains an NIH-defined experiment of Dual Use concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise such concerns either in confidential comments to the editor or in the review as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct remarks to authors vs confidential comments to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Although confidential comments to editors are respected, any remarks that might help to strengthen the paper should be directed to the authors themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve confidential comments for matters that cannot be shared with authors (e.g., sensitive competing interest disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability for re-review of revised manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are often asked to evaluate revised manuscripts and authors’ responses to reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors hope reviewers will make themselves available for re-review and questions from the editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing reviewers’ reports: do not edit or delete
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board members should not edit or delete reviewer reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If they have concerns about suitability of reviewer comments, they should notify PLOS staff before sending a decision letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLOS staff exceptions for editing reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS staff will not change reviewer comments intended for authors to read, except in cases where language is inappropriate for professional communication, or if comments contain information considered confidential or that would incur a major risk if conveyed to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is applied conservatively; contact PLOS staff with concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors may advise authors to disregard unreliable reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewer content concerns do not meet the strict criteria for editing, PLOS staff or handling editors may advise authors that they can disregard a reviewer’s comments in whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include concerns about the reliability of the feedback or alignment with journal standards or policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLOS will not edit reports after decisions delivered
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS will not edit or remove any reviewer reports for decisions that have already been delivered to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After decision delivery, PLOS staff may still inform authors if there are comments which do not need to be addressed in revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision process — editors make the final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors make the final decision on whether to publish each submission based on reviewers’ comments, the PLOS Pathogens criteria for publication, and their own assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' recommendations are considered but editors integrate all information, including material not made available to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers disagree fundamentally, editors may share all reviews with reviewers and request additional comments to help reach a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are not necessarily made by majority rule; editors evaluate recommendations alongside authors’ comments and other materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to get more peer review guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For more tips, use the Peer Review Center and Peer Review Toolbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact plospathogens@plos.org for questions or assistance submitting the review.
